newsitem.title: USA: Alumax unit to cut work force, consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Alumax unit to cut work force, consolidate.

text.p: Alumax Inc said Tuesday it will substantially cut the workforce and consolidate certain operations within its Alumax Engineered Metal Processes Inc.
The plan includes consolidating three existing AEMP facilities in St. Louis into one and making the Bentonville, Arkansas, plant into a satellite plant.
In addition, the AEMP work force will be "substantially reduced," the company said.
The business now employs about 525 people, but firm figures on the number of salaried and hourly jobs to be cut are not yet available, said company spokesman Daniel Loh.

Loh said the job cuts would take place during the next six months, beginning this month. He said the company is still evaluating the financial impact of the consolidation and could not give an estimate of possible charges.
The plan also transfers AEMP sales and marketing functions to Alumax Transportation Products in Chicago, and it establishes AEMP headquarters at the Jackson, Tennessee, plant.
The headquarters are now in St. Louis, Missouri, Loh said.
"The consolidation and action plan will put AEMP on the right track to profitable, commercial-scale production," said Jay Linard, president of Alumax Engineered Metal.
The company said total process control will be implemented throughout the company and that all existing business would be carefully reviewed and analyzed.
